name: Create your own TV channel
description: Your own TV channels in Jellyfin's Live TV, made from your films and series. Add your own branding with an corner logo, short title clips, transitions, Coming up next cards and coming-up trailers.
author: TheMightyTRexUK

settings.label: Station name
settings.hint: Shown in Jellyfin's Live TV and on screen. Up to 40 characters.

settings.label: Language
settings.hint: This sets the language of three things. The first is the words on the picture and in the guide, such as Coming up next and the day and time. The second is the sound track, where a programme has one in this language. The third is film and series titles and descriptions, which come from the film database.

settings.label: Picture size
settings.hint: The size of the stream while a channel is watched.

settings.label: Most channels at once
settings.hint: Each channel being watched is one server work. People watching the same channel share it.

settings.label: Stop a channel after the last viewer leaves
settings.hint: Nothing runs while nobody watches.

settings.label: First channel number
settings.hint: 1 puts your channels first in Jellyfin's Live TV, before the free channels from 101.

settings.label: Days in Jellyfin's guide
settings.hint: Worked out when Jellyfin asks for it, about once a day.

settings.label: Address Jellyfin uses to reach this plug-in
settings.hint: Filled in by itself: Starboard gives this plug-in its address on your home network, such as http://192.168.1.20:8790. Enter one only when Jellyfin reaches the server by another address.

settings.label: Copy programmes when nothing is drawn on them
settings.hint: A channel with no corner logo and no title bars plays its programmes as they are, with no converting.

settings.label: Leave out 3D films
settings.hint: A 3D film plays as two pictures. Films Jellyfin or their file name says are 3D are left out, and each film on a channel is checked once in quiet hours.

settings.label: Make coming-up trailers in quiet hours
settings.hint: Short clips of a programme coming up, with its sound, a background music and its day and time, on a background loop. One at a time, at the lowest priority, never while anyone is watching.

settings.label: Coming-up trailers kept for each channel
settings.hint: Old ones are replaced, so they never pile up.

settings.label: Replace each coming-up trailer after
settings.hint: A coming-up trailer is also replaced once its programme has started.

settings.label: Coming-up trailer length

choices.label: As the pack says (15 seconds unless it says otherwise)

settings.hint: How long each coming-up trailer is. Longer coming-up trailers show more clips. A change shows in the coming-up trailers made from the next quiet hour.

settings.label: Clips in each coming-up trailer

choices.label: By its length (about one every 5 seconds)

settings.hint: Short clips from different parts of the programme, clear of its opening titles and end credits.

settings.label: Use the programme's sound in coming-up trailers
settings.hint: Each clip plays with its own sound, at the same loudness as the rest, and the music goes quieter under it.

settings.label: Music under the programme's sound
settings.hint: How loud the music is while a clip's sound plays. It is at full before the first clip and after the last.

settings.label: Show the station's logo on coming-up trailers
settings.hint: The station pack's logo, small, in a corner of coming-up trailers made with a channel's own pack or a plain design. Coming-up trailers made with the station's pack carry it already.

settings.label: Audio description on coming-up trailers
settings.hint: A voice says each coming-up trailer's words: Coming soon, the title, the episode, the day and time and the channel. It adds the first sentence of the description when there is room. The music and the programme's sound fall under it. The voice is made on your server (eSpeak NG), in the station's language; nothing is sent anywhere. Coming-up trailers are made again in the next quiet hours.

settings.label: Show coming-up trailers for your other channels
settings.hint: Each channel's breaks show coming-up trailers for programmes on your other channels too.

settings.label: Corner logo
settings.hint: Every channel uses these unless it has its own, in Channels.

settings.label: Corner
settings.hint: Where it sits.

settings.label: Size
settings.hint: Small is 6% of the picture's height, medium 8.5% and large 12%.

settings.label: Distance from the edge
settings.hint: Inside the safe area keeps it on screen on every television.

settings.label: Opacity
settings.hint: 100% is solid.

settings.label: When it shows
settings.hint: Clips are short title clips, trailers and your own clips.

settings.label: Fades in after the opening
settings.hint: Keeps the opening titles clear.

settings.label: Clock
settings.hint: The time beside the corner logo.

settings.label: Label
settings.hint: In words, for the first 2 minutes of each programme.

settings.label: Dark box behind the logo
settings.hint: A dark, partly transparent box behind the logo, the clock and the label, so they are clear on any picture.

settings.label: Programme name at the start
settings.hint: For 8 seconds as each programme starts.

settings.label: Up next during the end credits
settings.hint: The next programme and its time, at the end of each programme.

settings.label: Coming up next and Later cards
settings.hint: In the breaks: the programme's picture, title, the date and time it is shown and a short synopsis.

settings.label: Channels
settings.hint: Add a channel and open it. It has a card for each part: its name and number, what it shows, what plays between programmes, what plays when, and more.

settings.label: What plays between programmes
settings.hint: Short title clips, clips, music and the waiting screen for every channel's breaks, with the break layouts and every file in one list.

settings.label: What plays when
settings.hint: Each channel's week on a grid, in a new tab on a computer, and what is on in the next 24 hours.

settings.label: Branding
settings.hint: Ready-made branding for the channels: try the example, add your own from the template, and set how things come on and go off.

settings.label: Choose a style for my channel
settings.hint: Add the video and picture files you made in Canva, Figma or another tool, or a zip of them, and turn them into your branding. Check each file, and say where it came from.

added: **Station break style** in What plays between programmes, with three styles: **Quiet**, **Classic TV** and **Busy**.
**Break style** on each channel's Breaks card says in words what the channel does, such as Uses the station style: Classic TV, and lets it use the station style, one of its own, or its own settings.
changed: The old break rows are under **More about breaks** on each channel's Breaks card.
Nothing changes until you choose a style. A channel saved before styles keeps every value it has.
The settings have fewer tabs: **Channels**, **What plays between programmes**, **What plays when**, **Branding**, **Station**, and **Logo, title bars and trailers**, then Actions.
**Streaming** is part of **Station**. **Guide** is inside **What plays when**. **Break layouts** and **File lists** are inside **What plays between programmes**. **Animation** is inside **Branding**.
Every setting keeps its key and its saved value.
**What plays between programmes** (it was Idents, clips and music) lists short title clips, clips, music, the waiting screen, then the more things, in that order.
The group called Add is gone: each group has its own add row and a one-sentence hint.
The hint on every upload says what to upload and no longer warns that names are not used.
added: **Use the example files** on an empty page, which adds ready-made branding with short title clips, a logo with music and a Coming up next card.

changed: Plain words for the television terms: **Short title clips** (idents), **Coming-up trailers** (promos), **Waiting screen** (holding slide), **Branding** (broadcast pack), **Title bars** (straps), **Corner logo** and **Public messages**.
A one-time explainer on each page says what a new word means, with the old word, and does not come back after you dismiss it.
Nothing you saved changes: every setting keeps its key and every channel plays as before.

added: **Lottie animations** in Import a kit: a Lottie file (JSON, up to 1 MB) can be a short title clip or a bumper. It is checked first (no expressions, links, pictures or text), its colours become your two colours, and your channel's name is drawn over it.

changed: **Turn on and turn off:** the text and the help pages now say turn on and turn off. How it works has not changed.

added: **Make a style here**: choose Clean, Evening, Retro, Bold or Plain, enter your channel's name and two colours, and add a logo if you have one. The plug-in draws 4 short title clips, 2 bumpers, the card and trailer backgrounds and the logo on your own server.

**A picture first**: a picture of a title clip, the Coming up next card and a bumper is drawn before any video. Nothing is made while anyone is watching a channel, with one FFmpeg thread at the lowest priority.
**Readable words**: a colour that would make the words hard to read is made a little darker or lighter until they reach 7 to 1. A still choice holds every clip still.
**The licence** is written into the pack: what the styles draw is free to use under the MIT licence.

**Choose a style for my channel**: a page, for a computer, that turns files you made in Canva, Figma, Descript or another tool into your branding. Add videos, pictures and sounds, or a zip, say what each is, say where each came from, and the plug-in makes the pack.
**A still picture becomes a short title clip**, 5 seconds that fade in and out, made on your server with one FFmpeg thread at the lowest priority and never while anyone is watching.
**LICENCE.txt and kit.json** are written into the branding, with where each file came from.
**A warning for fast flashing** on every clip made, added or imported. It says when a clip flashes more than 3 times in one second, and never stops you using it.

changed: Plainer wording in the text and help pages. How it works has not changed.
The copy of the design system's styles is current, with every theme and the latest components.

added: **Fit for Adverts**: in a break grid, Adverts can be set to Fit, which adds as many whole adverts as the break has room for. Nothing is cut short, and the holding countdown makes up the rest of the time.
**Break length for each column**: Automatic, or 2 to 30 minutes. A column whose items need more time says so in words, and the programme still starts on time.
**File lists**: one page for every ident, promo clip, advert and PSA, with search, sorting, filters, paging, and several files added to a channel or taken off it together.
**PSA**: a new kind of item for the break grids, with its own files, checked when added.
fixed: **The holding countdown and Back soon count what comes after them**: a bumper, promo or ident after them no longer makes the clock reach 0:00 early.

added: **Break grids**: two grids for each channel, In between programmes and Breaks, with up to 7 columns. Choose Random, Sequence, Day of week, or Morning, afternoon and evening, then drag items into the columns, or use the buttons and the keyboard.

**Where breaks go inside a programme**: at silence, at set times or at the end of a scene, and how many in each 30 minutes and in a film. Found once for each programme in the quiet hours, never while a channel streams.
A channel that has not changed its grids plays exactly as before.

**Audio description on promos** (not active unless you turn it on): a voice says each promo's words, so a blind viewer hears what is coming, on which channel, and when. It is made on your server, in the station's language. Nothing is sent anywhere.

**Language** (English unless changed): the words drawn on the picture and in the guide, such as Coming up next, Series and episode and the day and time, in English, French, German, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese, Dutch, Swedish, Danish or Norwegian.
**Sound track in your language:** a programme with more than one sound track plays the one in the station's language, else its default track.

**Titles in your language:** film and series titles, and film descriptions, are read in the station's language from the film database for programmes about to be shown, a few each hour, and kept. Episode names stay as Jellyfin has them.

fixed: **Moving a programme with the keyboard** on the schedule grid: focus goes straight to the programme at its new time, so a screen reader no longer reads the old time first, and the reason a move cannot be made is said once the actions have closed.

changed: **Busy buttons on the schedule grid** show a turning ring while Starboard works, such as Suggest a week, the same as the rest of Starboard.

fixed: **Reading the channels again updates each programme's details**, such as which sound track it plays, its title and its picture, even when the programmes are the same. The schedule does not change.
added: **Leave out 3D films** (Yes unless changed): a film Jellyfin or its file name says is 3D is left out of channels, and each film is checked once in quiet hours for two pictures side by side or one over the other.

fixed: **A programme with a subtitle file beside it showed only the channel's name card:** the plug-in asked for the subtitle in place of the sound. It now picks the sound among the file's own sound tracks.
**Pack logo check:** a busy plug-in no longer refuses a logo as having no transparent parts; it tries again, then says to upload the pack again in a minute.

added: **The station's logo on promos:** promos made with a channel's own pack, or a plain design, show the station pack's logo, small, in a corner. To leave it out, turn off Show the station's logo on promos.

fixed: **Promos follow a new pack:** when a channel's broadcast pack changes, its promos made with the old pack stop showing and are made again in the next quiet hour.
